A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IntrinsiX by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original FID evaluations, a participant study, component and dataset-size ablations, and generated image and scene-texturing results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports revised evaluations, an additional baseline, image-conditioned generation, rank sensitivity, and alternative lighting-sampling results.

M1.justification: The core two-stage LoRA training, cross-intrinsic attention, and rendering-loss procedure remain. Section 5.2 adds an image-conditioned variant by introducing RGB as another modality and applying conditioning dropout. Appendix B also introduces a BRDF-sampled training variant. These extend the method without replacing its main architecture.

E1.justification: The quantitative out-of-distribution evaluation changes from Hypersim indoor scenes and BlenderKit outdoor scenes to GObjaverse Daily-Used objects. This replaces the represented evaluation domain, rather than merely enlarging the same dataset. InteriorVerse training and the existing scene-texturing demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: IID, RGBX, and ColorfulShading remain. Table 1 and v2 Figure 15 add IID w/ FLUX-LoRA, trained with the same architecture and small dataset as the proposed method. Figure 15 also adds the image-conditioned IntrinsiX variant. ColorfulShading's additional mention in Section 5.1 does not establish new participation in Figure 6.

E3.justification: Section 5 expands the main InteriorVerse FID evaluation from 100 to all 2,595 test images and replaces the 40-image OOD evaluation with 1,000 GObjaverse samples. The new IID comparison controls backbone and training data. Reported user-study totals also change from 37 participants and 2,336 responses to 36 and 2,274, without explaining the revision. Appendix Table 2 retains its 100-image evaluation.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether pretrained PBR priors benefit image decomposition, compare LoRA ranks from 16 through 256, and investigate Disney BRDF lighting sampling. Appendix C adds an illustrated failure case concerning lost detail and incorrect normals. The previous dataset-size, diversity, stage-alignment, dropout, and rendering-loss analyses remain after matching their relocated figures.

E5.justification: Table 1 adds standard deviations to rendering-quality, specularity, and prompt-coherence ratings that previously had means only; the checklist identifies these as standard deviations. It also explicitly mentions different seeds for the retained diversity examples. Neither addition establishes more repeated training runs, and no confidence intervals or formal significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the main FID results under changed evaluation conditions: IntrinsiX's ID/OOD values change from 186.60/220.12 to 72.09/71.39, not a same-setting improvement. New results include IID w/ FLUX-LoRA at 103.36/79.29, image-conditioned OOD FID of 70.51, BRDF-sampled results of 75.26/68.87, and the rank sweep. The w/o CIA-Dropout specularity and prompt-coherence means change from 2.82/4.48 to 3.21/4.52. Dataset-size Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The probability definitions, flow-matching objective, attention formulation, and combined loss remain substantively unchanged. Equation (3) makes the incident-light argument explicit and expresses the cosine factor as a normal-light dot product, clarifying the existing rendering model. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about direct text-to-PBR generation, generalization, and the two-stage method remain. v2 newly claims first-time room-scale PBR texturing in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The introduction drops v1's assertion that direct generation eliminates decomposition ambiguity, replacing it with a claim about self-contained generation and generalization.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops the generalization explanation: matching an input image may distract decomposition models from learning the PBR distribution, while a pretrained PBR prior can benefit even image-conditioned decomposition. New limitations acknowledge reduced compositional diversity, lost detail, and incorrect intrinsic predictions relative to FLUX. Rank sensitivity and alternative lighting sampling also receive new interpretations and qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LoRA projection targets and documents CFG=10, flow normalization, and inverse-observation weighting for the existing scene-texturing application. It adds GPU memory, A6000 inference hardware, approximately 12-second sampling time, resource licenses, and user-study anonymity information. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. Code and weights are newly promised for release, rather than demonstrated to be available.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through material reconstruction and generation, including rendering-aware SVBRDF estimation, Material Palette, MaterialPicker, and concurrent diffusion-based G-buffer generation. It distinguishes independent priors and a fixed renderer from shared-ControlNet and diffusion-renderer approaches. Separately, the VFDS citation changes from the text-to-3D FlowDreamer work to a different robot-manipulation FlowDreamer paper, making that attribution questionable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most original prose remain. v2 makes localized introductory and application rewrites, improves several cross-references, reorders ablation discussion, and incorporates Individual PBR Priors into Appendix A. New appendix sections and a conference checklist extend the structure without a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds rank-sensitivity Figure 9, limitations Figure 17, and license Table 3. Table 1 gains a comparator row and uncertainty displays, while the supplementary albedo comparison gains two rows. Figure 5 is redesigned to show the input mesh and combined roughness/metallic panels. The existing dataset-size grid is transposed and relocated; most other imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: The matched FLUX-LoRA baseline and image-conditioned experiment address an important weakness in v1: differences in backbone and training data complicated its explanation of superiority over decomposition methods. Larger held-out evaluations, additional design tests, rating dispersions, and illustrated failures substantially strengthen the evidence and qualify the generalization claims. There are tradeoffs: the earlier scene-based OOD evaluation is replaced, the user-study count revision is unexplained, and the VFDS attribution becomes questionable. These issues limit the gains but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
